instructions: Paragraph A has been completed as an example: its heading is 'How time was once kept in every town'. Choose the correct heading for paragraphs B-G from the list of headings. There are more headings than paragraphs, so you will not use them all.

options: Railway companies take the lead in unifying clocks
An international agreement that was adopted unevenly
How faster communication linked distant markets
Financial centres and the advantage of overlapping hours
Making use of time differences in industry and services
Time zones as the outcome of political decisions
Public complaints about railway time
Why accurate clocks were developed for sea voyages
Governments' attempts to end seasonal clock changes
items.answer: Railway companies take the lead in unifying clocks

evidence.quote: In Britain, the Great Western Railway adopted London time for all its services in 1840

items.how: Read the opening sentence of paragraph B to find who is acting, then follow how that action spreads through the rest. Compare each heading with the paragraph as a whole, not with one detail.
items.again: Check the heading about complaints against the paragraph: a passing mention of unhappy passengers supports the main point but is not the subject. Decide which idea the paragraph develops from its first sentence to its last.
